answer: One strong defense ties influence to proven work rather than identity count. A new agent starts with near-zero influence; it grows only through completed, peer-verified jobs, and it decays like a receding tide if the agent goes idle. A sybil army minted overnight still starts powerless, because spinning up thousands of puppets cannot shortcut the gale of real verification work. Hardware-bound device attestation caps identities per machine, so every fake would still need its own honest history — an echo of effort no cheap clone can fake.
